text:
(TN) A friend mentioned my name shows up as a “person of interest” at my university, connected to xanax sales. Everything I keep comes from a prescribing specialist and stays in a lockbox—antidepressant, atypical antipsychotic, alprazolam, adderall. Hospital screenings matched only what’s expected, with nothing extra found. No police record, always open and respectful with university officers, and I’ve even reported safety concerns before.

Selling any of my medicine has never happened. I once spoke to others about having alprazolam from my specialist but shared little beyond that. Hearing from a friend that I appear on this type of list is really raising my anxiety. Should I hire someone qualified to guide and defend me, or do I continue life as I have been if I’m not involved in what campus police suspect? How do I handle being named in this situation?

I’m doing part-time work alongside my studies. It’s been almost two full cycles since I started, and payment arrives as discussed, but there is no paperwork in place. When I bring this up, our hr person mentions paperwork is still getting drafted, since I am their first person in this kind of role. What possible issues could come up if nothing is signed or formalized in this setup?

I get 9 dollars for each hour where I work in Illinois, but the lowest allowed wage went up to 9.25 after January 1. I have been working there for around 5 cycles and my hourly wage stayed the same. How do I get my hourly wage increased to meet the updated required minimum?

Minnesota tenant move-out and deposit basics:

I picked up a duplex last spring and have been living in the downstairs space. The folks upstairs moved in about 4-5 springs back, and their current rental contract wraps up in late May. They’ve mentioned possibly leaving when that wraps up.

The previous owner mentioned a no-smoking policy for the building, but their earlier rental contract didn’t lay that out. When we went through paperwork for their current stay, it spells out no smoking inside.

I’m sure they smoke inside quite a bit—smoke drifts into the stairwells, and one of them admitted to it directly. It doesn’t really bother me. There’s no carpet, and the rest of the space stays fresh. Still, if they do move when May wraps up, I will really need to repaint all the walls and ceilings—about 1300 sqft. Their security deposit sits at $850. Would it fall within Minnesota rules to label smoke odor as more than everyday use and hold back some of the deposit to cover the paint job?

Signed up for a small gym not owned by a large chain, with a promise to send $9.00 every four weeks for twelve cycles, and my dad filled in the forms since I wasn’t at the required age yet. The money always came straight from my own checking spot. The forms mention that missing a scheduled transfer by more than ten cycles means extra charges show up, and the business can ask for the full total up until you completely cancel. Payments move through something called ABC Financial Services.

After enrolling, I only saw the first transfer go through—nothing else happened for a while. I got concerned the owner would catch on and pile on extra charges. Every transfer was supposed to happen with the information I gave when signing up, not exchanged in person. Checked again and saw most of the transfers did go through, but one or two regular transfers seem missing. Should I expect extra charges or other troubles now, or is this for the owner to sort out? What should I do next?

My boss at the hotel won’t hand over the paper I need for HMRC to sort out about £200 that came off my pay as tax and national insurance by mistake.

I’m 20 and studying in England. Last financial cycle, I worked three separate places—nightclub, bar, hotel. The bar delayed sorting my work details, so tax and NI were taken from my pay until HMRC received the right info. HMRC said I’d see the refund after a short time, but nothing happened. By the time things closed for that cycle, I still hadn’t seen it. When I phoned again, someone at HMRC checked and saw the hotel still had me on the records but never sent a P60, so my full pay for that work never showed up for HMRC.

Later, after the pandemic cut off all my work and I struggled to cover my place, I reached out to the hotel manager asking for my P60 to show HMRC. No response. She finally replied later, saying she’d sent one by email, but I checked and nothing was there. Sent another message—again, no reply. The hotel isn’t a big chain, there’s nowhere I can drop in, and I haven’t stepped in there in ages, yet I’m still on their employee files.

How do I fix this? Can HMRC keep that refund forever if my boss never gives the paper? I try calling HMRC but never get through. If anyone here has tips for sorting this (with HMRC or my boss), please reply. I need this refund, especially as a student with bills.

Who has the job of clearing out a person using a separate living space above a garage at a home in NJ, inherited by a son who lives in PA? A lawyer is handling the relative’s matters. The space has been used free of charge for a long time by someone who could cover costs but refuses.

Is it up to the person settling the estate to move this person out before handing over the home to the inheritor?

(North Carolina) I got let go by my workplace during the Covid-19 shutdown. After about a month and a half, my boss offered a spot to return, or to stay home if needed. I let him know I would be safer waiting another week or two. He replied with “At your convenience.” After about seven days, I texted to ask if I should come back soon as things in the workplace seemed to be starting up. He then let me go for “refusing to come back.” What is the correct way to answer on the Unemployment application when it asks whether I left a job?

My homeroom teacher is giving us a penalty every time someone is late to class, their shirt is untucked, if they swear, or for things like poor manners. When this happens, we roll a dice and have to hand over the amount in coins that comes up, with everything collected going to charity. If someone breaks 3 rules, they have to stay after school for detention on Friday. There are 24 of us in the group, and this rule only happens in our homeroom—no other groups in the school get this penalty. Can a teacher set something like this up where only certain students get this kind of penalty, especially since giving anything for charity should be a choice? This is happening in Victoria, Australia.

My partner’s father died by suicide in a small Minnesota town over two months back. The body was sent to Minneapolis for an autopsy. Both the sheriff’s office and funeral home repeat that they’re still waiting on the medical examiner. Updates only come if we call — always the same: it’s not done.

We still do not have the official paper showing he is dead, and without it, foreclosure on his place and his debts cannot be handled, and nobody can touch any funds left behind. We are in a different part of the country, so only phone calls are possible.

Does it usually take this long for situations like this in Minnesota, or does such a delay point to a possible mistake or carelessness? Can anything be done to make the process go faster or force action? What steps could we try to get this paperwork finalized?

I have a well-known blog focused on guides and reviews, and there’s a business from Shenzhen with a bad reputation among my readers for unreliable practices. Even though this group has a polished internet presence, user stories paint a clear picture of issues affecting many people. My posts often show up at the top when someone searches on Google.

I am thinking about sharing critical feedback on this group so others can be informed about these reports. My main concern is whether talking about these complaints—most of which come from personal stories and things I’ve seen on the web—could cause trouble for me, like claims that I’m harming someone’s reputation. I live in Florida, and this group is based in China.

Is there anything important I should consider so I can get this information to my readers without putting myself at risk?

Prepare a letter meant for a judge.

Situation: My former spouse strangled me while our children were nearby. The former spouse agreed to a plea deal for this, but did not finish what they agreed to. At the sentencing, the other side’s representative brought up a paperwork mistake, and the judge allowed more time to finish the deal. Since then, over several first Thursdays, hearings about the strangling have been scheduled.

Concerns: I am upset about how lenient things have been, because my former spouse still harasses me, stalks me, and tries to control what I do. The abusive treatment continues. I do not have anyone to stand up for me in these matters. The judge should know about the ongoing abusive actions, because everything is connected. My former spouse even stalked and harassed someone I started seeing after finding out about them.

Request: Draft a letter for the judge that explains all of this clearly, strongly asking that the continued harassment and abuse be dealt with as part of the original strangling incident.

Warehouse job in Illinois ended with "unprofessional behavior in the workplace" after an argument with a supervisor that happened outdoors, after everyone else had gone, and not during working time. Applied for unemployment benefits but think the company will challenge for misconduct.

No earlier warnings, never disciplined, nothing repeated or intentional. Supervisor was the first one to raise their voice. The whole thing took about half a minute, not inside, and not while working.

HR never checked my side before letting me go. The company is a large shipping warehouse with frequent problems and lots of people quitting or being let go. Stress and gossip are the norm there.

I have a medical record for manic depression and severe anxiety, and put this in my application—some supervisors knew. My temper can get away from me at times.

Rules for Illinois unemployment mention misconduct as purposely breaking rules, causing actual harm, or doing the same thing after being told to stop. My situation didn’t happen during a shift, didn’t harm anyone or anything, wasn’t repeated, and I have no negative history.

Let me know what kind of chance there is for being given unemployment after this, what usually happens in these cases, and if telling them about my medical history might lead them to view what happened differently.

Pulled over in Wichita, Kansas for expired tags—plates were nearly a month late and officer noticed they were on a vehicle without registration. Officer handed out a slip to come in, not a fine. Plates became mixed up after a transfer from parents; previous ones ended up on the vehicle again by mistake and never went through the renewal.

Tomorrow is the scheduled appearance. Looking for a quick outline of what the process might look like or what to bring, since this is the first time dealing with this and stress levels are high.

My wife and I are separating and discussing care arrangements for our child. We are dividing time with the child equally, but she wants to have all the major decision-making power. I am very unsure about letting this happen, and she is saying she will bring this to a judge if I do not agree.

Can a person who hurt someone else spend a shorter period locked up if the reason for the action makes sense and is understandable? 

Tell me.

Is it against rules in Pennsylvania to let people tour a place when smoke alarms are not on the ceiling or wall? I’ve had visitors while alarms were missing because earlier people took them down and put one on the counter where anyone could spot it. I always explained that cleanup and repairs were still happening before someone new could move in, including replacing carpet because of pet mess. Someone thinking of living there might have told local officials about the alarms. I plan to put the alarms back up before anyone else looks at the place. Could showing it without alarms in place bring problems?

My Kansas place was broken into two times. After that, I moved out 3 months before the rental agreement was supposed to finish and the person who rented the place to me knew about it. The rental agreement ended 21 before now. When I moved, there was a small hole in the wall, nothing big, but now I’ve been sent a repair document with a charge of $940, including some custom trim that didn’t exist before. Can I request a different quote or get a quote from someone else? I went through the Kansas rules and read Goodeill vs. Madison Real Estate, but I’m still not sure what protections are available in this situation. Can you break down what options apply here? Here are the Kansas rules and the decision:

[Kansas Legislation](http://www.kslegislature.org/li_2012/b2011_12/statute/058_000_0000_chapter/058_025_0000_article/058_025_0108_section/058_025_0108_k/)

[Goodeill vs. Madison Real Estate](https://www.courts.wa.gov/opinions/pdf/324427.pub.pdf)

Teacher with a visa for teaching from overseas. A detective wants to talk after someone brought up a claim about me (I have no details yet). I have a professional for defense set up, and I hope everything will show I’m not connected at all.

If everything shows I was accused for no reason, then what usually happens? I’m anxious my workplace or district could still let me go, even if I did nothing — a professional said this is possible. I’ve heard of teachers who went back to their classrooms after leave, but the whole situation leaves me uneasy.

What safety do workers from outside the country actually get in these cases? I moved from another place to be a teacher here, and now it seems like I could lose everything I moved for because of one claim (if there’s a minor as the claim says). What steps can I take if the school removes me even after everything is cleared up? Is a single claim really enough for them to let a teacher go, even once it’s been shown I did not do anything?

Is there someone who can speak up for those in my position, to stop a school from removing an educator harmed by something untrue? Can a school let a person go with no proof from a record that’s now clear? What can I do as someone on a visa if this happens?

I hope what the professional said about being found clear and still losing my place is not true. That would be worse than the claim itself. I’m buried under all of this, especially thinking about my loved ones. Any pointers about where I stand in this kind of situation would be deeply meaningful.

Left my job due to unsafe conditions and took my situation to the Labour Board in NS for what I was owed. Both parties signed a settlement and release. Cheques were issued, sent to the Board, and paperwork held until funds were confirmed. I put all three cheques into the bank at the start of April. At the same time, I started Peace Bond proceedings against the other person. After the first hearing, that person emailed to say the cheques would be stopped.

Is it even possible to stop the cheques after both parties have signed the agreement and the cheques have already been put into my account? Feeling overwhelmed and looking for guidance on what to do in Nova Scotia, Canada.

What could result if someone chooses not to follow through after putting their signature on a letter describing their intent to accept a job? 

I put my own signature on this type of letter, getting ready to begin June 1 in Virginia. My current place is stressful and difficult, but the next one should offer a more relaxed pace and lighter load. Approval for escorted building entry has wrapped up, but I’m feeling uneasy about not having completely final clearance and worrying the offer might be withdrawn. My background is clean, so maybe I’m just thinking too much.

Are there possible consequences for me if I back out after making this commitment on paper?

Suspected negligence by building management?

Around five months before now, someone forced open the garage door at my building, and about twenty expensive vehicles ended up with missing parts. No security cameras were set up in the garage, even though a lot of us living here asked for them after this happened.

Last night, my motorcycle disappeared from inside the same garage while I was sleeping. I checked in with management and let them know the time window when the bike was last seen (between 9 PM and 4 AM). They told me maintenance staff noticed someone taped the sensor to keep the garage gate open. I brought up the earlier thefts again and pushed for cameras. The reply was that “COVID-19 has kept us from hiring anyone to put cameras in.” This didn’t seem believable to me, since I see workers regularly coming in to upgrade the pool and gathering space.

The rental contract states personal losses or damage are not covered, and management is not required to add extra protection for the garage. Meanwhile, residents are charged more for electronic entry fobs and for using covered parking spots.

They know about several missing items from the garage but no extra protection has been set up or changes made. Does this situation fit the definition of negligence?

Illinois – small business closed its office and sent out a message to all staff: any unpaid wages for tasks already finished will be mailed once they either get an SBA disaster loan or start up again, whichever of those comes up first. My position depended on places currently closed due to COVID, so there have been no clients, and the business has stopped running. The office closed on 3/16, and our last paid stretch wrapped up then. Afterward, they told everyone by group message: “All back wages will be sent in full once we are approved for the SBA disaster loan or when normal business begins again (whichever happens before the other).”

No one is picking up new shifts, so working for future wages is not happening. Do they have permission to put off sending checks for completed tasks based on these reasons? Does applying for the SBA disaster loan allow them to not send out wages on time? There have been no SBA developments or official details, and the last message said reopening will not happen until sometime much later, with no mention of our checks.

I already put together an email requesting what is owed, but need to check one more time that the business has no legal permission to delay sending wages. Illinois rules require all wages from completed tasks to be mailed out no later than 13 calendar markers after the end of the pay stretch for every two weeks, or 7 calendar markers for week-by-week pay. Staff placed off shift by layoff or strike should have wages mailed on the next regular wage day. Their messages say they follow all workplace rules for COVID and I have already checked wage requirements, so I am fairly certain, but really need a final double-check before sending my message.

How does support for raising a child go in Mississippi?

Two summers back while passed out and drunk, I was assaulted and the woman involved became pregnant. Out of embarrassment, I did not speak about it. I gave her $300 each period as support, handing it straight to her. Later, she mentioned pursuing adoption, so I helped her try, but no placement happened. Later, a letter arrived from Mississippi, naming me and asking me to appear before a judge. I called the number given in the letter, and the person who answered said not to turn up—instead they only wanted to see if I was the father. They said a home kit would come through the mail, but it never reached me. Four more turns of the calendar passed. Last period, another letter came in, saying Mississippi would begin support actions against me. I called again, but no one at the number could find anything using my details. I wrote to the woman who assaulted me to ask what was going on, and she messaged that I must send $600 every four weeks. I told her that figure would ruin me, and she responded that $400 every four weeks would be enough. Then, earlier today, she messaged again and said Mississippi required I pay for her vehicle bill and her vehicle protection—she described this as a needed thing for parents without the child in their care in Mississippi. She said I could keep sending $400 and add $165 extra for protection. I searched but cannot find anything about this being needed by rules from Mississippi. I am trying to save for someone with training in defense but my account is shrinking. Share what a person in this position should do next, and if that vehicle protection is truly needed for raising a child in Mississippi.

My mom runs a small shop in Miami, Florida. A friend who later joined her as a partner became very controlling. She always wanted to know my mom’s location, who she spent time with, and became upset if my mom did not reply right away. She often asked for my mom's email password, but my mom never shared it. When my mom left her phone at the shop, she would return and find it locked after someone kept entering the wrong password, which seems like this woman tried to unlock it more than once.

Things became much more tense. The partner once went into the shop, yelled at my mom, and demanded she leave. Earlier, while my mom was nearby, this woman rushed out to confront her. She brought printed copies of emails and messages that must have come from my mom’s private info. My mom never let her see anything like this. The partner’s son works at T-mobile, and this seems like the only possible way she could get access to those messages.

My mom feels overwhelmed and unsure where to turn. The partner has displayed threatening behavior in the past. I am looking for information about what steps my mom should consider next, especially because the whole situation feels like a violation of her privacy and possibly not allowed under Florida rules. Any information is welcome.

Need info about leaving a Massachusetts rental very soon after a long-term commitment is signed. Here’s the situation: the paperwork was done, move-in happened, and within a handful of mornings, conflict between dogs led to an immediate exit.

Initial and final payments along with a security deposit have already been paid, and those funds are assumed gone. But now the person in charge of the place is insisting that the signed commitment still holds, even though the tenant is no longer staying.

Is there any path for getting out early if move-out takes place almost immediately—like less than a week in? Can ownership actually take someone to court and have a chance of winning more? Wondering about usual outcomes in cases like this.

At my school in Estonia, all students were gathered for an event during lesson time. It was presented as a discussion on healthy eating, but instead the group of speakers encouraged everyone to try Vemma, a drink connected to a pyramid scheme. They spoke about earning money and shared stories of people whose lives changed after getting involved. The room included those who are below the legal limit for certain purchases. Is it permitted for a commercial pitch like this to be held at a school for minors during class? If not, which school official or group would be responsible for letting it happen?

(CA) How do you make a relative move out of your place when you never put together a written rental deal?

My mother moved in with me and my wife in August. Things were calm at first, similar to how she acted in her previous place where she stayed for three trips around the sun. She followed the rules we set ahead of time. Now things have gone downhill—she smokes inside (I have health issues from growing up and cannot handle smoke), has burned the carpet, leaves food that’s been sitting around under the bed and sink, keeps her room dirty, and ignores all of the rules we agreed to.

My wife and I cannot stay with this anymore and need her to leave. We already let her know she needs to find another place to stay by the last day of October, and after that she is not welcome to come over.

We are fine giving her 400 every four weeks for a dozen cycles to leave and not return.

If she does not accept, do we have to go through any kind of formal process to force her to leave our place?

(Wisconsin) Water soaked my ceiling and ruined several textbooks in my university dorm

I sleep in a dorm at a university in Wisconsin. My room is a single, and I share a bathroom with one other person. At 4 in the morning on Thursday, February 5, I woke up to water pouring into my room from two corners of the ceiling. My fridge, microwave, much of the floor, and four textbooks all wound up soaked. My neighbor across the shared bathroom also had water leaking onto his side. We put out containers and called campus security. They brought a hall director from another building, who checked on people above us and then returned. We kept cleaning up with our own bath towels and newspapers, but water remained everywhere. I took plenty of photos of my books, and my neighbor took photos too. When campus staff returned, they told us the people above us had left their window open with the heater on, which led to a pipe breaking. Maintenance switched off the water and the dripping stopped.

The hall director asked for our names and asked if anything we owned was wet. I described my ruined textbooks, and my neighbor mentioned his television, Xbox One, Nintendo 64, and other electronics were soaked too. The director said to keep cleaning. They tried to bring us towels but did not locate any, then left, saying someone else would clean soon. Nobody came to assist. We finished cleaning at about 6 in the morning using all our own towels and newspapers. A staff member dropped by at 7 in the morning to mop, but we had already completed the job.

The next evening around 8, water leaked again—less than before, but still hit my heater and counter. We called for assistance and were met by the same staff and two security people. This time they took a few photos and checked upstairs before maintenance stopped the water again. Staff said someone would mop, but no one arrived.

Now I am trying to understand if my university followed the rules for this kind of thing. Should my neighbor or I expect anything for our ruined things? Two and a half fortnights have passed with no word or apology. If I should expect some replacement, who should I talk to at the university?

**Summary: Water leaked into my dorm and soaked my books and belongings. No communication from campus about repairs or replacing anything. Can I expect repairs or payment for ruined things, and if so, who do I contact on campus, especially since so much time has passed with no reply?**

Meaning of "distribution" in rules and what could happen for someone who receives something

Location: United States, New Hampshire

If a rule talks about trouble for people who produce or send out a certain thing, does that include the person who gets or uses it? From what I see, if the rule does not mention having the thing as an issue, then it looks like only the person who produces or sends it out could face trouble—not the one who only gets or uses it. But I have not found anything written out in plain language anywhere to be sure of this.

If posting this breaks a posting rule, sorry

Risk of losing my bread and butter TX, USA

I repair machines in Texas. I’m 22. I put my name on an agreement without checking what was inside, and it turns out this paper blocks me from opening my own place, fixing things for anyone else, or even doing repairs in this field for five entire trips around the sun if I step away.

Is there any way a person in my shoes could avoid this rule?

Roommate let a stranger move in while I was away for college in Iowa. After summer at home, I returned to find someone I did not know in my space. Roommate gave permission for this person to be there, and the office at the complex did not say anything to me. The stranger broke things, and I moved out before the agreement was supposed to finish. During this time, my roommate died. I stopped sending payments to the office for the two cycles after moving out, thinking my deposit would cover damages.

Now almost eight cycles later, I saw something pop up when I tried to get another place. A collections group claims I owe an amount.

How can I handle this? Is there any way to have this removed from my record with the credit organizations without paying what they claim?

Can someone get arrested in Palo Alto, CA for one prank call?

Here is the background: I reached out by phone to a person who used to manage a group project I joined. There was no signed agreement, no payment, and after spotting online that he removed me and another musician from the group website with no heads-up, I called him pretending to discuss his patent and referenced a “NOTICE OF APPROVAL OF EXTENSION REQUEST E-MAILED.” This person also holds contact details for my parents and knows where I sleep. I did this in a moment of frustration after discovering he picked a different computer expert without telling me.

Let me know if more information is needed.

My roommate’s parents own the place where I’m staying, and I signed a rental contract with them in Lincoln, Nebraska, starting in May 2014. We have been here for about five cycles, and my roommate told me her parents plan to move us to a different place because they hope to sell this one. The agreement does not mention anything about switching places early, and I never agreed to a move. If they ask me to leave this spot for a different one, does that end my rental contract?

[USA] Forcing former spouse to sell shared home in Louisiana

Here’s the situation. My mom and her former husband both have their names on a house. He ended up in prison some time back and my mom separated from him. The house was not dealt with during the separation since he wasn’t around.

He owes both my mom and me a lot of cash because we gave him support after he got out of prison, trying to keep things peaceful. Now, my mom covers the mortgage alone, and he refuses to sell the house or settle up with her for her part.

Is there a way to force a sale of the house or get something set up so he would have to buy out my mom’s share? This is all in Louisiana.

Hired someone with law training to try to avoid losing my ability to drive after rolling past a stop sign in March. Pulled over while following GPS, only given a citation for the stop sign. Two earlier citations for driving too fast in the past twelve periods meant I needed to complete driving retraining, and was informed another traffic offense would mean losing my permission to drive.

Chose to say not guilty for the stop sign citation, trusting that paying for a law specialist would mean no suspension, considering it would cost less than higher insurance rates. Met with the specialist at the government building, who suggested changing my plea to a phone use offense, which should have been costlier but would not lead to loss of driving permission by itself, since I never had that type of issue before. Followed this plan, but soon after, received a letter saying permission to drive was taken away. After reaching out to different places, I learned that any new moving offense after retraining sets off the penalty. Now the person who offered their service will not reply, even after saying more calls would be made to find out if anything else could be done. Hoping for clear guidance: is it reasonable to ask for my $500 back here? If there’s no refund, should I submit a complaint with those who supervise law professionals?

Is it possible for someone you share a rental with in Michigan to get you to sign a different contract to stay in the unit? Here’s what’s going on: splitting up, and he cannot move into his own place in the same mobile home park unless his name disappears from the current rental document. Been in this place for five trips around the sun, so renting is on a rolling basis.

He’s asking me to fill out forms so only my name appears, but I cannot cover costs or meet requirements until support payments start. He is reaching out to the owner by himself and suggesting there could be removal if I do not go along with it.

Can he cut off the rental agreement or transfer the mobile home to someone else without me, or is there any way for him to force me out?

Stopped in Pennsylvania at 79 in a 55 zone, handheld radar used and checked on 12/22/2014. Officer adjusted it down to 60 in a 55, which set the fine at $35, but extra fees brought it to $138.50 total. The officer said no points would show up and spoke politely about changing the charge. This is my first situation like this, and I really hope nothing appears on my driving record. Should I show up to traffic proceedings and ask for something better, or move forward with the current fine since no points show up? Also, will my rate for driving protection change if there are no points added?

[PA/NY] Our first son went to live with relatives through adoption close to ten years back. I am now married to my partner and we share another child together. The son who went to live with our relatives has severe autism, does not speak, and needs a lot of assistance every day. Since December, the relatives who took him in have been reaching out by message and phone, telling us to "take responsibility" and "contribute more," suggesting that because he has many needs, we should either bring him to live with us or support them. The only record we have is a few written messages with these words. We have seen our son only twice at family events since the adoption, which was meant to be partly open.

We do not have enough resources to give him the level of care he needs, and our son went to live with the relatives from birth through the courts. Are we required to do anything, financially or otherwise, in PA or NY? We have stopped replying so we do not mistakenly create any kind of agreement.

The contract I signed for the place where I’m staying includes wording at the top about last payment being settled in advance and held with my security deposit. The person in charge of the building phoned to say that section was added in error and told me that last payment isn’t covered, and I should still send in this final amount. The dollar amount written for last payment is also $70 lower than my usual amount.

I’m not clear about whether last payment really was given earlier, but since it’s listed in the signed paperwork, I thought it would count. Does that protect me in any way, or can the person in charge still request more money even though the paperwork says the last payment is taken care of?

This is about a place in St Louis, Missouri.

Stayed with someone in Sweden who offered a place to sleep free for a short period (Jan 18 to Jan 23). When it was time for me to pack up, this individual demanded 500 SEK or threatened to hold onto my things—computer, university assignments, and more. Nothing was written and the property owner later mentioned that for the same period he only would have asked 166 SEK.

Reasons given for requesting funds included using the refrigerator without asking, using toothpaste without permission, and claims about my use of cosmetics (but they added there was no accusation of theft). They also brought up that I didn’t offer food in return, but when I tried to cover drinks or meals my offer was refused.

After I handed over the money, no receipt was given. All conversation about staying free happened over Facebook with message copies and timestamps, but now I am blocked and can’t see the rest. The property owner supports my version. There are people who can confirm I stayed there. I have no evidence for handing over cash, no contract, only those messages.

Is there anything to do next in this situation?
